content:
.TH GENESIS-MATH 7 "November 2026" "Genesis 0.2.0" "Genesis Manual"
.SH NAME
genesis-math \- the parietal mathematics faculties of the Genesis mind
.SH SYNOPSIS
.nf
\fBParietalMath\fR                 parietal faculty facade
\fBparietal_lobe.math.algebra\fR   symbolic expression trees
\fBparietal_lobe.math.calculus\fR  differentiation and integration
\fBparietal_lobe.math.statistics\fR descriptive and sampling statistics
\fBparietal_lobe.math.symbolic\fR optional SymPy verification oracle
.fi
.SH DESCRIPTION
Genesis's parietal lobe contains a family of mathematical faculties,
not one monolithic calculator. The native faculties represent and
manipulate expressions, matrices, permutations, relations, graphs,
geometric objects, and propositions. They are exposed through the
.B ParietalMath
facade in
.I python/parietal_lobe/math/__init__.py .
The package also has corresponding Rust mathematics modules under
.IR src/math/ .
.PP
The native algebra and calculus faculties operate on Genesis's own
expression trees and rule systems. They do not delegate their
mathematical work to an external language model or computer-algebra
system. The separate
.B symbolic.py
module is an optional SymPy-backed oracle used to check claims and
support research provenance; it is not the implementation of all
the native faculties.
.SS Foundational faculties
.TP
.B Number sense
.I number_sense.py
implements approximate magnitude comparison, subitizing,
estimation, Weber--Fechner scaling, and plausibility judgments.
These are approximate judgments, not exact arithmetic.
.TP
.B Arithmetic
.I arithmetic.py
parses and evaluates arithmetic expressions using an explicit
recursive-descent evaluator. It accepts numeric expressions, number
and operator words, common spoken fractions and mixed numbers, decimal
phrases, percentages, and square-root expressions. It does not use Python
.BR eval() .
.TP
.B Algebra
.I algebra.py
parses expressions into immutable trees for constants, variables,
negation, sums, products, powers, and elementary function calls.
It simplifies to canonical form, combines like terms and factors,
expands products, evaluates expressions, and solves supported
equations. The parser supports implicit multiplication such as
.IR 2x ,
.IR 3(x+1) ,
and
.IR (x+1)(x-1) .
.TP
.B Calculus
.I calculus.py
differentiates expression trees using constant, sum, product,
quotient, chain, power, and elementary-function rules. It computes
supported antiderivatives, definite integrals, slopes at a point,
and Taylor polynomials. Definite integration falls back to composite
Simpson quadrature when the antiderivative rules do not find a
closed form.
.TP
.B Statistics
.I statistics.py
provides central tendency, dispersion, distribution shape, and
sampling summaries:
.IP \(bu 2
Central tendency: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic, generalized
power, quadratic, cubic, contraharmonic, Heronian, Heinz, Lehmer,
median, mode, midrange, and trimmed means.
.IP \(bu 2
Dispersion: population or sample variance and standard deviation,
mean absolute deviation, median absolute deviation, percentiles,
percentile ranges, interquartile range, coefficient of variation,
and data range.
.IP \(bu 2
Shape and sampling: raw and central moments, skewness, kurtosis
(raw or excess), standard error, and
.B sampling_means()
for repeated samples with replacement.
.PP
The Heronian, Heinz, and Lehmer means are two-value functions; they
are not members of the
.B mean()
dispatcher. The dispatcher accepts exactly
.B MEAN_KINDS:
.IR arithmetic ,
.IR geometric ,
.IR harmonic ,
.IR quadratic ,
.IR cubic ,
.IR contraharmonic ,
.IR power ,
.IR median ,
.IR mode ,
and
.IR midrange .
The
.B summarize()
facade reports population variance and standard deviation.
.SS Higher mathematical domains
Each domain has a Python faculty and a corresponding Rust module
under
.IR src/math/ .
.TP
.B Trigonometry
.I trig.py
handles angle expressions, degree/radian conversion, trigonometric
ratios, exact names for common special angles, and triangle solving.
.TP
.B Linear algebra
.I linear_algebra.py
parses explicit matrix and vector literals. Matrix operations include
transpose, addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, matrix
multiplication, determinant, rank, inverse, trace, and unique
square-system solving. Vector operations include addition, subtraction,
dot product, and three-dimensional cross product. Elimination and
vector arithmetic use
rational
.B Fraction
arithmetic, preserving exact rational results for supported inputs.
Inverse and trace require square matrices; inverse additionally
requires nonsingularity. Vector operations require matching dimensions.
.TP
.B Abstract algebra
.I abstract_algebra.py
parses permutations in cycle notation and computes composition,
inverse, cycles, order, parity, orbits, and generated subgroups.
Subgroup generation is bounded by a configured cap.
.TP
.B Real analysis
.I real_analysis.py
provides numerical limit exploration, sampled function graphs,
Riemann sums, Simpson quadrature, and bisection. Its epsilon-delta
challenge uses finite numerical probes; it is not a formal
universal proof over every real point.
.TP
.B Complex analysis
.I complex_analysis.py
parses complex values in rectangular, pair, and cis notation and
computes magnitude, argument, polar descriptions, integer powers,
nth roots, and roots of unity.
.TP
.B Number theory
.I number_theory.py
provides primality checks, prime factorization, greatest common
divisors with Bezout coefficients, modular inverses, congruence
solving, Euler's totient, and the Chinese remainder theorem.
.TP
.B Topology
.I topology.py
works with finite topological spaces: validates topology axioms,
computes closure and interior, and evaluates Euler characteristics
and simple finite-space invariants.
.TP
.B Geometry
.I geometry.py
computes point distances, polygon areas and orientation, point-in-
polygon membership, and convex hulls from coordinate data.
.TP
.B Discrete mathematics
.I discrete.py
checks finite relations for reflexivity, symmetry, antisymmetry,
transitivity, and equivalence; it also explores graph connectivity
and reachability.
.TP
.B Combinatorics
.I combinatorics.py
counts combinations, ordered arrangements, multinomial
arrangements, derangements, and Stirling partitions without
enumerating every arrangement.
.SS Mathematical foundations
.TP
.B Axioms
.I axioms.py
checks finite binary-operation tables for closure, associativity,
identity, inverses, and commutativity. It classifies the resulting
structure along the magma, semigroup, monoid, group, and abelian
group ladder, retaining a witness when an axiom fails.
.TP
.B Propositional proof
.I proof.py
represents propositions built from atoms, negation, conjunction,
disjunction, implication, and biconditional. It checks truth tables,
tautology, satisfiability, entailment, and named inference rules;
invalid entailments can return a countermodel. This is a
propositional proof faculty, not a general first-order theorem
prover.
.SS Symbolic oracle and research workbench
.B symbolic.py
is backed by SymPy and imported lazily. It can be unavailable when
SymPy is not installed; the native algebra and calculus modules do
not depend on that optional package for their own operations.
.PP
The oracle supports symbolic simplification, expansion, factoring,
cancellation, partial fractions, rational-expression combination,
trigonometric simplification, differentiation, integration,
equation solving, limits, series, numerical evaluation, and matrix
determinant, eigenvalue, trace, inverse, and characteristic-
polynomial operations.
.PP
Equality and inequality checks return
.IR verified ,
.IR refuted ,
or
.IR undecided .
A bounded equality check that passes every tested integer remains
.IR undecided ;
a finite range is not promoted to a proof. An undecidable claim
stays unverified.
.PP
The
.B ResearchWorkbench
in
.I python/frontal_lobe/research.py
persists open mathematical problems, conjectures, readings,
empirical evidence, and recorded attempts under
.IR $DATA_DIR/research/workbench.json .
Only an oracle verdict can give a claim terminal
.I verified
or
.I refuted
provenance. Bounded checks can refute with a witness or add
evidence, but cannot verify a universal claim merely because all
tested points passed.
.SH ENTRY POINTS
.TP
.B ParietalMath
The parietal faculty API. Its domain methods are reached from the
frontal mathematical entry point through
.I parietal_lobe.math.cognitive.route_parietal_math .
Explicitly supported language forms dispatch to native number sense,
arithmetic, algebra, calculus, statistics, trigonometry, linear algebra, abstract algebra,
real analysis, complex analysis, number theory, geometry, discrete
mathematics, combinatorics, topology, axiom-classification, and
structured propositional tautology/satisfiability faculties.
Unsupported or underspecified forms are not guessed.
.TP
.B parietal_lobe.math
The package-level exports, result types, and domain detectors.
.TP
.B parietal_lobe.math.symbolic
The optional symbolic oracle used for claim verification.
.TP
.B frontal_lobe.research
The persistent mathematical research workbench.
.SH FILES
.TP
.I python/parietal_lobe/math/
The native mathematical faculties, their cognitive router, and the optional symbolic oracle.
.TP
.I src/math/
Rust mathematical modules corresponding to the parietal domains.
.TP
.I python/frontal_lobe/research.py
Persistent research threads, claims, evidence, attempts, and oracle
verification.
.TP
.I python/tests/test_higher_math.py
Tests for the native algebra, calculus, and higher mathematical
faculties.
.TP
.I python/tests/test_higher_math_cognition.py
End-to-end tests proving that the frontal math entry point reaches
selected native parietal faculties.
.TP
.I python/tests/test_research_math.py
Tests for symbolic verification and the research workbench.
.TP
.I python/tests/test_statistics.py
Tests for statistical measures and sampling behavior.
.SH LIMITATIONS
The frontal reasoning entry point calls the parietal cognitive router
before the narrower arithmetic/algebra solver. The router supports
only explicit operation forms implemented in
.I python/parietal_lobe/math/cognitive.py .
Foundational arithmetic includes numeric and number-word expressions,
spoken addition/subtraction/multiplication/division, common fractions
and mixed numbers, decimal phrases, percentages, halves, doubles,
triples, squares, cubes, square roots, powers, parenthesized
order-of-operations expressions, and magnitude comparisons. Linear
algebra language supports explicit matrix literals for determinant,
rank, transpose, inverse, trace, addition, subtraction, scalar
multiplication, matrix multiplication, and unique square-system
solving, plus explicit vector literals for addition, subtraction,
dot products, and three-dimensional cross products. It does not
automatically infer omitted matrices or vectors. The cognitive router also accepts
angle conversions (for example, 180 degrees to radians), triangle
side triples, complex nth-root requests, linear congruences in the
form ax ≡ b (mod m), Euler totients, and Chinese remainder systems
as explicit lists of (residue, modulus) pairs. Geometry accepts a
point literal followed by polygon vertices for point-in-polygon
queries. Discrete mathematics accepts explicit edge-pair literals
for graph connectivity. Combinatorics accepts Stirling S(n,k)
questions and stars-and-bars counts with explicit object and bin
counts.
This is not unrestricted mathematical language understanding: each
domain still requires its documented operand syntax, and a missing
operand produces an honest failure rather than an invented value.
The propositional-proof faculty currently accepts structured
proposition trees; it does not parse arbitrary natural-language
proof statements.
.PP
Algebraic solving has supported closed-form cases and a numerical
root-search fallback; a numerical root is an approximation.
Integration uses a finite rule table and numerical quadrature when
no closed antiderivative is found. Real-analysis limit exploration
uses finite numerical probes, not a proof over the continuum.
.PP
The optional SymPy oracle is not the source of the native
faculties, and it is not a complete proof assistant. Propositional
truth-table checks, finite algebraic-structure checks, symbolic
identities, and numerical evidence each have their own scope.
Unsupported or undecidable claims must remain unverified.
.SH SEE ALSO
.BR genesis (1),
.BR genesis-cli (1),
.BR genesis-reasoning (7),
.BR genesis-vision (7)

.TH GENESIS-MATH 7 "October 2026" "Genesis 0.2.0" "Genesis Manual"
.SH NAME
genesis-math \- the parietal mathematics faculty of the Genesis mind
.SH SYNOPSIS
.nf
\fBparietal_lobe.math.number_sense\fR  approximate magnitude (ANS)
\fBparietal_lobe.math.arithmetic\fR    exact symbolic calculation
\fBparietal_lobe.math.statistics\fR    descriptive statistics
\fBparietal_lobe.math.symbolic\fR      SymPy-backed manipulation
.fi
.SH DESCRIPTION
The parietal lobe is Genesis's number cortex, modelled on the
intraparietal sulcus (IPS): the region that encodes quantity before
any symbolic procedure. The faculty is layered the way the anatomy
is layered.
.PP
.B number_sense.py
is the approximate number system \(em subitizing, Weber-Fechner
magnitude comparison, estimation, and plausibility checking. It is
the intuition underneath: it judges whether a quantity
.IR feels
bigger and flags answers that violate magnitude intuition.
.PP
.B arithmetic.py
is exact symbolic calculation \(em a recursive-descent evaluator
over digits, symbols, and number/operator words
.RI ( "7 + 5" ,
.IR "nine times eight" ).
No
.BR eval() :
each step is explicit so arithmetic errors are traceable the way a
person's slips are.
.PP
.B statistics.py
describes collections rather than single quantities \(em where a
sample's center is, how widely it scatters, and what shape it has.
Three families:

.SS Central tendency
The named means. The Pythagorean three \(em
.IR arithmetic ,
.IR geometric ,
.I harmonic
\(em sit on the power-mean ladder
.RI ( "(\(*Sx^p / n)^(1/p)" ),
alongside
.I quadratic
.RI ( p =2),
.I cubic
.RI ( p =3),
and
.I contraharmonic
.RI ( "\(*Sx^2 / \(*Sx" ).
The two-value interpolating family
.I ( heronian ", " heinz ", " lehmer )
smoothly connects the classical cases; Lehmer's ladder recovers
arithmetic, geometric, harmonic, and contraharmonic at integer and
half-integer
.IR p .
.IR median ,
.IR mode ,
.IR midrange ,
and
.I trimmed_mean
complete the set.
.SS Dispersion
.IR variance
and
.I standard_deviation
(with Bessel's correction for samples),
.IR mean_absolute_deviation ,
the fully robust
.IR median_absolute_deviation ,
.IR percentile
and
.IR percentile_range /
.IR interquartile_range ,
.IR coefficient_of_variation ,
and
.IR data_range .
.SS Shape
Raw and central
.IR moments ,
.IR skewness
(tail direction),
.I kurtosis
(tail weight, with an
.I excess
convention so the normal reads 0), and
.IR standard_error .
.I sampling_means
draws the empirical sampling distribution of the mean \(em the
central limit theorem demonstrated on the data rather than asserted.
.SH ENTRY POINTS
.TP
.B ParietalMath
The facade the rest of the mind talks to:
.BR looks_like_math () " and " looks_like_statistics ()
classify a question;
.BR evaluate () " computes arithmetic;"
.BR mean ( values ", " kind ", " p )
dispatches over
.BR MEAN_KINDS ;
.BR summarize ( values )
returns a
.B StatSummary
(center, spread, and shape in one pass).
.TP
.B parietal_lobe.math.statistics
The module itself when the measures are needed individually.
.SH FILES
.TP
.I python/parietal_lobe/math/
The package source.
.TP
.I python/tests/test_statistics.py
The taxonomy under test \(em the mean inequality, both ladders, the
CLT demonstration.
.SH SEE ALSO
.BR genesis (1),
.BR genesis-cli (1),
.BR genesis-reasoning (7)
